summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, and Bangabasi College. He held lectureships at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, and Patna College (1912), becoming University Reader at Patna University in 1923.

Johan Elverskog specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at UC Berkeley (B.A. ~1991–1993) and Indiana University (M.A. ~1993–1995). Since ~2001, he has served as a professor at Southern Methodist University.

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Utrecht University, Leiden University (doctorate under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865) and Leiden University (1865–1903).
Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1901 to 1924 and at Leiden University from 1924 to 1933.

Johan Huizinga worked in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at the University of Groningen (~1891–1895) and Leiden University (~1895–1896) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later held posts at Groningen (1905–1915) and Leiden (1914–1942).

Johann Andreas Schmeller worked in linguistics after studying at the Wilhelmsgymnasium (~1801–1803). He taught at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1817–1826), became a Kustos at the Bavarian State Library (1829), and held professorships at the University of Munich (1828, 1846).
Johann Caspar von Orelli worked in linguistics. He held academic posts at the Cantonal School of Graubünden (~1807–1819), Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christoph Adelung worked in linguistics. He studied at Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). He later served at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and as head librarian at Saxon State Library Dresden (1787).
Johann Elias Schlegel was an academic who completed his studies at Schulpforta (~1733–1739) and Leipzig University (~1739–1743).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1765–1769), the University of Jena (~1769–1772), and the University of Göttingen (~1772–1775). He subsequently spent his career as a faculty member at the University of Göttingen (~1776–1840).
Johann Friedrich Herbart worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Jena from ~1794 to 1797 and subsequently held a post at the University of Göttingen from ~1802 to 1841.

Johann Friedrich Pfaff studied at Karlsschule Stuttgart until 1785 and at the University of Göttingen (1785–1787). He held academic posts at the University of Helmstedt (1788–1810) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1810–1825).

Johann Gildemeister was an Indologist. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and at Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, Christian Lassen, and A.W. Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (~1845–1859) and the University of Bonn (~1859–1890).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen (1770–1774). He held professorships in oriental languages at Jena (1775) and philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Greifswald (1808) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1812). He held professorships at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850).

Johann Gottfried von Herder worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg under Immanuel Kant (1762–1764). He held posts at Riga Cathedral School (1764–1769), Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium (~1776–1803), and as General Superintendent at Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (1776).

Johann Gustav Stickel specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena under J.G.L. Kosegarten (~1823–1827) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1828–1830), later serving as professor at Jena (1830–1836).

Johann III Bernoulli worked in history/archaeology and related fields. He studied at the University of Neuchâtel and earned a doctorate from the University of Basel (~1757–1758). He was a member of the Prussian, Imperial, and Danzig academies.
Johann Jakob Engel was a philosopher. He completed his studies at the University of Rostock (~1757–1762) and Leipzig University (~1762–1764).

Johann Joachim Winckelmann worked in history and archaeology. He received his education at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1736), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1738–1740), and the University of Jena (1741–1742).
